d: Paired mucus-secreting glands at about 4 and 8 o'clock in the posterior vestibule that lubricate the introitus. A blocked duct forms a cyst, and infection makes an abscess.
Vaginal squamous cells so coated with Gardnerella and other bacteria that their borders look stippled. They are one of the four Amsel criteria for bacterial vaginosis.

A chronic T-cell-mediated skin disease with thin, white, parchment-like skin. On the vulva it forms a figure-of-eight around the vulva and anus, spares the vagina and carries a small cancer risk. On the penis it scars the foreskin and glans, causing pathologic phimosis.
The HPV-independent vulvar precursor, with atypia confined to the basal layer, aberrant p53 staining and absent or patchy p16. It arises in lichen sclerosus and leads to keratinizing carcinoma.
An intraepithelial adenocarcinoma of the vulva, with large pale PAS-positive cells in the epidermis. Unlike Paget disease of the nipple, it usually has no underlying carcinoma.
The grape-like form of embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, a bleeding vaginal mass in girls under 5. Its small round blue cells form a cambium layer and stain for desmin and myogenin.
